name: Nevyn
sources: Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. (New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972), 42.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nevyn is a figure of Welsh folklore. She was a mermaid who lived in the sea off the Carnarvonshire coast. A young man, Ivan Morgan, held her dear. She made a devoted and loyal wife and gave him two children, the boy Nevydd and the girl Eilonwy. The family lived well until Nevyn grew homesick for the land beneath the waves. While the parents visited that underwater world, Nevydd came to know his true line and died from the shame of it. Eilonwy tried to drown herself out of grief, but a handsome merman prince rescued her and took her to live with him under the sea. Nevyn turned back to the shore. She carried off the body of her son on a ship that came by magic. The tale does not say what became of the grieving Ivan. The name Nevydd resembles Niamh of the Golden Hair, the Irish fairy queen, and the two figures may once have been the same.

okr.objective: Nevyn is a Welsh mermaid whose love for Ivan Morgan ended when she returned to her home beneath the sea.
key_results: Nevyn was a mermaid beloved by the young man Ivan Morgan on the Carnarvonshire coast.
She bore a son, Nevydd, and a daughter, Eilonwy, and lived happily until homesickness struck.
Nevydd died of shame after learning his heritage, and Eilonwy was rescued from drowning by a merman prince.
Nevyn claimed her son's body and carried it away on a ship that appeared by magic.
